item.title: Crisis is child welfare: Some C-K kids been housed in Linck building
item.description: The demand for highly specialized care for some children, unable to be cared for by their parents, has exceeded available resources at times, which has led to eight youth being housed, at various times for extended periods, at the Linck Child, Youth and Family Supports office in Chatham. item.title: Chatham Christian going to OFSAA; Ursuline, Pain Court fall short

item.title: Rare Disease Day a celebration for Chatham teen living with ALGS
item.description: Saturday marks Rare Disease Day and Chatham teen Chord Jaques, who is among the estimated 300 million people worldwide living with a rare condition, has plenty to celebrate. Diagnosed at age two with Alagille syndrome (ALGS) after being born with a cholestatic liver — a rare condition that affects about one in 30,000 to 50,000 […]

item.description: CK Public Health issued an another alert Friday afternoon about an increase in drug poisonings (overdoses) and unexpected reactions to substances in Chatham‑Kent based on elevated opioid-related EMS calls during the last several days. “There are reports about the presence of strong tranquilizers in the local drug supply resulting in heavy sedation,” the health unit […]
